summary: Operator scripts, contracts tooling and root configs area S1 batch (22-25 Task 3, D-16 area-batch tier), presented once the SCRIPTS (10 files), CONTRACTS (8 files) and ROOT (19 files) slices were audited at audit base 23a6461 with their ledgers, the SCRIPTS and CONTRACTS sweeps, the ROOT sweep contribution, the SCRIPTS thresholds inventory and cards SCRIPTS-01..03 complete. One new S1 entry: AUD-SCRIPTS-002 (section C SC-12 / D4, LOSS) the operator scripts that sign with the bot wallet (scripts/deliberate-buy.ts through src/bot.ts:558 and :746-747, scripts/recover-sell-ladys.ts :70 and :78-80, and behind the broken RC-27 imports scripts/addLiquidity.ts :35-58 and scripts/deploySepoliaTest.ts :22-61) run as separate processes outside the bot nonce lock (a module-level Map per process, src/utils/nonceAuthority.ts:41-43) and never read the pause switch, so with the bot running on the same wallet both can sign with the same nonce or sell the same tokens. Presented with it, as the plan requires (D-STOP-THE-LINE: a premise challenge is put back to the operator, never filed and left): the D-06 premise question on card SCRIPTS-01 (How do out-of-process signing scripts exclude the running bot?). D-06 in 22-CONTEXT.md says the query API for Phase 29 scripts is try-acquire-then-release; that query takes the single-instance lock and lets it go again before the script signs, so the bot can start and take the lock in the gap (a check-then-act race); card SCRIPTS-01 recommends instead that a signing script holds acquireProcessLock (plan 22-13) for its whole run and checks the pause state while holding it. Options offered: hold-lock, query-then-sign, decide-in-phase-29, decimal-phase, stop. No S0, no rail, test-origin-db-row or non-public-secret item was found in these three slices: the Hardhat real-network signing accounts and the real .env load are recorded as a boundary (AUD-CONTRACTS-001, S2) and no test, fork or CI path reaches a real-network signer. The bot is OFF for all of v7.0, so nothing can happen now. Nothing is changed in Phase 22 (NAC-13): the fix is owned by Phase 29 (HYG-03). The operator was asked to rule on the signer-exclusion question and acknowledge the S1, or ask for a decimal phase, or stop the phase.
presented_at: 2026-11-07 session (after commit 97c7ae5 at 2026-11-07T20:26:10Z UTC): the 22-25 Task 3 blocking checkpoint (checkpoint:decision, gate blocking-human), relayed to the operator by the execute-phase orchestrator
operator_response_channel: typed by the operator at the 22-25 Task 3 blocking checkpoint; relayed verbatim by the execute-phase orchestrator to the 22-25 continuation executor, which recorded it at operator_response_recorded_at
acknowledgement_evidence: not required (operator_response is the operator's own verbatim reply, kept exactly as typed). Presented at presented_at through the 22-25 Task 3 blocking checkpoint (gate blocking-human).
ruling: decide-in-phase-29, in the operator's words "Acknowledge. Decide in phase 29": the S1 AUD-SCRIPTS-002 is acknowledged (severity stays S1, no decimal phase is inserted, Phase 22 continues); the signer-exclusion question on card SCRIPTS-01 (the D-06 premise challenge) is NOT resolved now and is handed, undecided, to the Phase 29 (HYG-03) discussion, which must rule on it before the script changes are planned; the D-06 wording in 22-CONTEXT.md is not changed now; card SCRIPTS-01 stays open with the hold-lock recommendation on record.
ruling_option_text: decide-in-phase-29: Acknowledge and decide in the Phase 29 discussion. Pros: the decision is made with the HYG-03 design in front of you. Cons: the card stays open until then.
ruling_note: Interpretation recorded as relayed by the orchestrator: "Acknowledge" acknowledges AUD-SCRIPTS-002; "Decide in phase 29" selects the decide-in-phase-29 option for the D-06 signer-exclusion question. No severity was changed, no decimal phase is inserted, and Phase 22 continues. Context, attributed to the execute-phase orchestrator and NOT to the operator (shown to the operator with the checkpoint): the orchestrator recommended hold-lock as the only option that closes the race, noting that the scripts are rare one-off tools, so "stop the bot first" costs little; it noted that hold-lock matches card BUY-01's refuse-while-running-and-prompt option ("refuse while the bot runs, then tell you to start the bot"), and that if BUY-01 instead becomes handoff-to-running-bot ("hand the buy to the running bot"), no separate script signs at all for the deliberate buy; it called query-then-sign the one to avoid because it gives false assurance. The operator chose to leave the decision to Phase 29 with the full HYG-03 design in front of them. Card BUY-01 is owned by the Phase 24 capital discussion, which comes first, so Phase 29 rules on SCRIPTS-01 knowing the BUY-01 outcome. As an S1 capital finding, AUD-SCRIPTS-002 cannot rest on the keep-current default; it blocks the live re-entry gate until it is decided and fixed.
